cases.name: division-published-example
cases.description: The Division's own example company: $1,000,000 gross assets, 485,000 issued shares, 1,000,000 authorized at $1.00 par plus 250,000 at $5.00 par. Authorized Shares Method on 1,250,000 shares bills $10,790; Assumed Par Value Capital Method carries $1,000,000 / 485,000 to six decimals ($2.061856), builds $3,311,856 of assumed par value capital, rounds up to 4 million, and bills 4 × $400 = $1,600, saving $9,190.
cases.source: Delaware Division of Corporations, "How to Calculate Franchise Taxes" published examples (https://corp.delaware.gov/frtaxcalc/, verified 2026-10-01); 8 Del. C. § 503

cases.name: authorized-shares-cheaper
cases.description: The comparison going the other way: 1,000 authorized shares with $50,000,000 of gross assets. The default Authorized Shares bill is the $175 minimum; the assumed-par method reaches $20,000 (assumed par $50,000, capital $50,000,000, 50 × $400), so the default bill wins by $19,825.
